# internal-ca-trust

Make containers, language runtimes and headless browsers trust a private certificate authority (step-ca or any internal root) so they can reach internal HTTPS services, without dropping the public roots. Covers fetching and fingerprinting the root, the system store for root and non-root images, Python (requests, certifi, httpx, aiohttp), Node, git and curl variables, Chromium and Playwright, ACME clients such as Traefik's lego, and the checks that prove it worked. Use when a container or tool fails with "certificate verify failed", "unable to get local issuer certificate" or "self-signed certificate in certificate chain" against an internal hostname, or when a stack must start calling internal HTTPS services. Do NOT use to run or configure the CA itself (issuing, provisioners, renewal), for public certificates from Let's Encrypt (use traefik-lan-routes), or to switch TLS verification off.

## Install

Copy this directory into either skills location, then start a new session:

```bash
cp -r internal-ca-trust ~/.claude/skills/       # personal, all projects
cp -r internal-ca-trust .claude/skills/         # this project only
```

For Claude Desktop, zip the directory and upload it under
Settings, Capabilities, Skills. Released builds attach a ready-made zip.
